statements.text: Great to talk with 103.7 FM about the NDAA, Mountain Valley Pipeline, and what's happening with AI. Check out our conversation here: https://t.co/QiN31MekWf
President Trump announced an aggressive artificial intelligence plan to keep the U.S. competitive with China.
statements.context: Floor speech in the U.S. House of Representatives advocating for energy infrastructure development to support AI competitiveness.

statements.text: AI is the defining technology of the next several decades. It will have a revolutionary effect on all aspects of our lives. It will be integral in everything from high-level data analysis to the use of a search engine. [...] This is just the beginning of the capabilities that AI will give us, and it is why it is critical that the US leads the way in the deployment of this technology.
statements.venue: House Energy and Commerce full committee hearing on AI and energy (excerpt in committee press release)

statements.text: Here in the U.S., we see similar challenges unfolding with the patchwork of State AI laws rapidly taking shape. Just since January, there have been over 1,000 AI bills introduced across the United States. These measures vary widely in their definitions, in their requirements, their enforcement mechanisms, and in their scope.
statements.venue: House E&C Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade Subcommittee hearing 'AI Regulation and the Future of U.S. Leadership' (opening statement delivered by Joyce)

statements.text: To be clear, I am not advocating for a free-for-all wild-west-type regulatory environment. On Monday, Chairman Guthrie was proud to stand with President Trump as he signed the TAKE IT DOWN Act. This law is a prime example of targeting a specific harm with a narrowly tailored law to fill a gap that has been identified in existing law.

statements.text: Madam Speaker, this week, President Trump will join Senator Dave McCormick in Pittsburgh for the inaugural Pennsylvania Energy and Innovation Summit. Discussed the potential of AI to transform the delivery of healthcare during today's @HouseCommerce Health Subcommittee hearing.

As Chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, I held a hearing on the risks and benefits of AI chatbots.

As AI continues to be developed and integrated into our everyday lives, it is important that we establish guardrails to ensure the safe use of these technologies—especially when it comes to protecting children online.

Click here to watch my opening remarks: https://t.co/1HJ1SgLCsq

Click here to watch my line of questioning to the witnesses: https://t.co/TolFvxiPEG

Second, chatbots are designed to maximize engagement with users. As a result, sycophantic chatbots have been found to affirm harmful or illogical beliefs, providing vulnerable users with perceived support for unhealthy behaviors such as self-harm, eating disorders, and suicide. For children and adults with a propensity for mental illness, this can be particularly problematic.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House E&C Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee hearing on AI chatbots

statements.text: My goal today is to have a balanced, frank conversation about the potential benefits and harms of AI chatbots to Americans. It is important that we consider the implications of these technologies as we balance the benefits of AI innovation with protecting the most vulnerable among us.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House E&C Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee hearing on AI chatbots

statements.text: I’ve been leading the charge against the potential harms of AI. [...] It’s no secret that these chatbots, they’re a significant but unique harm to kids. So I think we need a framework, a federal fame framework that fosters innovation but protects our kids, and not a state by state patchwork

As a physician, I must acknowledge the extraordinary promise that AI-enabled biotechnology holds for patient care. AI is accelerating drug discovery, improving protein modeling, and enabling the development of therapies with unprecedented precision.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House E&C Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee hearing on AI and biosecurity

statements.text: But the same technological advancements can also raise the stakes for biosecurity. These risks are not theoretical. National security experts warn that adversarial nations—including China, North Korea, Iran, Russia, and others—may seek to exploit AI-enabled biological design tools for malicious purposes. We must take those warnings seriously.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House E&C Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee hearing on AI and biosecurity
